_README: Single source of truth for what each shift contains.
Edit this file, then run: python3 tools/gen_days.py
That rewrites data/days/day_*.tres, which is what the game loads.
tools/smoke/smoke_content.gd fails if the two ever disagree.
A day says WHAT IT CONTAINS in one of two ways:
mix   - how many items land in each bin, e.g. {"organic": 5, "landfill": 3}.
The generator picks real items whose category resolves to that bin
UNDER THAT DAY'S RULES, round-robining in id order so the same JSON
always expands to the same list. Add a new item to data/items and
re-run gen_days.py and it joins the rotation automatically.
Bins: organic, recyclable, hazard, landfill.
"exclude": [ids] keeps specific items out of the draw.
items - an exact list, when a day has to hold still. Wins over mix.
Day 1 uses this: smoke_upgrade_play measures grip on whatever the
seeded shuffle puts first, and only items heavier than 0.333 leave
the grip chance unclamped, so day 1's contents are pinned by hand.
The bin an item belongs in is decided by that day's rules, so the same id can
be RECYCLABLE on day 1 and LANDFILL on day 2 - which is why mix is resolved
per-day rather than once globally.
spawn_interval_min/max: seconds between arrivals once the opening
items are down. min_available_items: if the tank drops to this many,
the next item arrives immediately instead of waiting.

days.intro_text: First day. Sort on what you can see - there are no inspection tools yet. Every drop, inspection and sort spends shift time; thinking is free.
The inspection tools arrive. Rinse to find residue, magnifier to read codes. Both spend shift time.
The chem swab is available. Not all residue is equally dangerous.
The cutter is available. What looks like paper is not always paper - but every inspection eats into your drops.
More rules and more items, on nearly the same shift time. Watch for the new foil rule.
